headline: The US jobs report at 16:30 Dubai was weaker than forecast on every count, US bond yields fell and markets all but dropped the chance of an October Fed rise, so the dollar eased. GBP/USD jumped from 1.3205 to 1.3250 at the release, gave back about half within minutes and was near 1.3226 at 17:40 Dubai, helped too by oil falling below $100 (about £76).

happened.result: Employers added 29,000 jobs against 90,000 expected, and July and August were revised down by a combined 60,000. Unemployment rose to 4.2% against 4.1% expected, and hourly pay rose 0.1% in the month against 0.3% expected.
happened.why: A cooling US job market and slower pay growth make another Fed rate rise less likely; Reuters reported that US two-year yields fell 7 basis points to 4.716% and ten-year yields 6 basis points to 5.176%, and the market chance of an October rise fell to as low as 12%, so the dollar weakened and GBP/USD rose.
happened.effect: GBP/USD jumped from 1.3205 just before 16:30 Dubai to a high of 1.3250 in the first minute and 1.3236 two minutes later, slipped to about 1.3219 by 16:33, and has since moved between about 1.3212 and 1.3241. It was near 1.3226 at 17:40 Dubai, about 0.15% above its level before the report, taking GBP/AED from about 4.850 to about 4.857.

happened.result: Trading Economics reported on Friday that Brent fell about 3% to around $99.30 (about £75.10), as European governments considered releasing strategic oil and fuel reserves to ease fuel costs and Middle East crude flows recovered towards pre-war levels. This reverses most of Thursday's jump on the carrier report.
happened.why: Cheaper oil eases inflation worries and the pull of the dollar as a safe haven, which tends to help the pound against the dollar, so each pound buys slightly more dirhams.
happened.effect: The time of the move is not known. The fall in oil came on the same day as the weaker US jobs report, and GBP/USD stood about 0.3% above Thursday evening's low near 1.3183 by 17:40 Dubai.

happened.event: Dollar eases slightly in the European morning before the US jobs report
happened.result: FXStreet reported at about 11:15 Dubai that the dollar index had slipped back below 102.00 after reaching 102.20 on Thursday, its highest since April 2025, with GBP/USD slightly above 1.3210, up about 0.2% on the day. There was no UK data this morning, and FXStreet reported that the chance of an October Fed rise priced by markets had fallen to about 24%, from over 70% a week earlier.
happened.why: Traders tend to trim their dollar holdings before a big US report after a strong run, which lets the pound recover a little, so each pound buys slightly more dirhams.
happened.effect: GBP/USD rose from about 1.3205 at 07:00 Dubai to a high near 1.3218 at about 10:30 Dubai, then settled near 1.3208 by 12:30 Dubai, taking GBP/AED from about 4.850 to about 4.854 and back to about 4.851.

happened.result: The National reported on Friday that Brent eased 0.05% to $102.10 (about £77.30) and US crude 0.31% to $92.58 (about £70.10), as larger Saudi shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, 2.9 million barrels a day in September against about 1 million in August, balanced the US carrier deployment. OPEC+ meets on Sunday to set November output.
happened.why: Steady oil removes one source of fresh demand for the dollar, though prices above $100 (about £76) keep inflation worries and US yields high.
happened.effect: The time of the news is not known. Oil's pause matched a quiet morning for GBP/USD, which stayed between about 1.3200 and 1.3218.

happened.event: Sterling near its lowest since June in Asian trading
happened.result: FXStreet reported GBP/USD below 1.3200 in Asian trading on Friday, near its lowest since 26 June, with the dollar index near 102, its highest since spring 2025, and traders waiting for the US jobs report. Brent rose a further 0.3% to $102.60 (about £77.70), Reuters reported.
happened.why: With US yields high and oil dear, money has kept flowing into the dollar, so each pound buys fewer dirhams; quiet trading before a big report tends to hold the rate near its lows.
happened.effect: GBP/USD eased from about 1.3195 at 03:30 Dubai to a low near 1.3180 at about 05:35 Dubai, then recovered to about 1.3204 by 07:35 Dubai, taking GBP/AED from about 4.840 back to about 4.849.

happened.event: Report of a third US aircraft carrier for the Middle East lifts oil
happened.result: The Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday that the US is sending the USS Theodore Roosevelt strike group to the Middle East, with up to 10,000 more troops, and a US official confirmed the deployment to The National. Brent for December settled up 4.4% at $102.31 (about £77.50) and US crude up 2.7% at $92.87 (about £70.40).
happened.why: Dearer oil and the risk of renewed conflict with Iran push up inflation worries and US yields and draw money into the dollar as a safe haven, so each pound buys fewer dirhams.
happened.effect: The time of the report is not known. GBP/USD slid from about 1.3226 at 18:45 Dubai to about 1.3207 at 19:05 Dubai and to a low near 1.3183 by 19:50 Dubai, then settled near 1.3190 through the evening.

happened.result: 54.5 against 55.0 expected and 54.6 in August, the ninth month of growth in a row. The prices paid index jumped to 77.9 from 71.1, and the employment index rose to 52.7 from 51.2.
happened.why: A slightly softer headline would normally weaken the dollar, but the sharp rise in prices paid points to more inflation, which keeps a Fed rise in play and supported the dollar.
happened.effect: GBP/USD fell from 1.3234 just before the release to about 1.3221 within five minutes, then held near 1.3225 for the next half hour.

happened.event: UK 30-year borrowing costs pass 6% for the first time since 1998
happened.result: The 30-year gilt yield briefly reached about 6.03% on Thursday and the 10-year gilt yield moved above 5.50%, its highest since 2007, amid worries about energy-driven inflation, heavy government borrowing and the Budget on 28 October. The FTSE 100 lost 177.73 points.
happened.why: When UK yields rise because investors worry about the public finances, rather than because the economy is strong, the pound tends to fall with gilt prices, so each pound buys fewer dirhams.
happened.effect: This weighed on sterling through Thursday alongside the firmer dollar; GBP/USD fell from about 1.3263 early on Thursday to about 1.3190 by the evening.

happened.result: 197,000 new claims in the week to 26 September, against about 201,000 expected, the lowest since July. Continuing claims fell to 1.701 million.
happened.why: Fewer people losing their jobs points to a strong US labour market, which normally keeps a Fed rise in play and supports the dollar.
happened.effect: GBP/USD edged up from 1.3228 just before the release to about 1.3235 within two minutes, as sterling had already fallen a long way that morning.

drivers.title: US bond yields
drivers.text: The US 10-year yield reached about 5.34% on Thursday 1 October, near its highest since 2002, then fell 6 basis points to about 5.18% on Friday after the weak jobs report, Reuters reported. High US yields keep the dollar attractive to hold and remain the main weight on sterling.

drivers.title: UK borrowing costs and the Budget
drivers.text: The 30-year gilt yield passed 6% on 1 October for the first time since 1998, and the 10-year rose above 5.50%. With the Budget due on 28 October, worries about the public finances are weighing on the pound as well as on gilts.

drivers.title: Fed rate expectations
drivers.text: Reuters reported on Friday 2 October that the market chance of an October Fed rise fell to as low as 12% after the jobs report, from about 24% that morning and over 70% a week earlier. September added 29,000 jobs against 90,000 expected and unemployment rose to 4.2%. Thursday's ISM prices index at 77.9 still shows inflation pressure. The next Fed decision is on 28 October.

drivers.title: Oil and the Middle East
drivers.text: Brent settled at $102.31 (about £77.50) on 1 October after the report of a third US carrier for the region, then fell about 3% to around $99.30 (about £75.10) on 2 October as Europe weighed releasing reserves. OPEC+ meets on Sunday 4 October to set November output, and oil remains sensitive to news on Iran.

drivers.title: The Bank of England
drivers.text: The Bank held Bank Rate at 3.75% on 17 September, with three of the nine members voting for a rise, and FXStreet reported on 1 October that markets price as many as four rises by next summer. At about 1.3226, GBP/AED is near 4.857 at the peg of 3.6725.

lower: US inflation or wage figures next week stronger than forecast, which would revive the chance of a Fed rise on 28 October and strengthen the dollar.
UK long-dated gilt yields rising further on worries about the public finances before the 28 October Budget, which would weigh on the pound.
OPEC+ cutting output on Sunday, or oil climbing back above $100 (about £76) on news of escalation with Iran, which tends to strengthen the dollar.
US 10-year yields climbing back towards Thursday's highs, which would keep drawing money into the dollar.
higher: Further signs of a cooling US job market or softer inflation next week, which would keep an October Fed rise off the table and weaken the dollar.
Europe confirming a release of oil reserves, or progress in the US talks with Iran, which would keep oil lower and reduce the demand for dollars.
Gilt yields easing back from their highs, which would relieve the pressure on the pound.
Bank of England speakers pointing to a rise on 5 November, which would lift the pound.
watch: OPEC+ meets on Sunday 4 October to set November output; a cut would tend to lift oil and the dollar, and an increase would help someone selling pounds for dirhams. Next week's US and UK calendar appears in the table below once it is published.
